scenarios.rationale: Based on 2024 industry averages for mid-market firms. Severity includes ransom payment, recovery, and business interruption.
High frequency, moderate severity. Primarily reflects business email compromise (BEC) and data theft impact.
Lower frequency but high 'tail risk' (Sigma 1.8) due to the range of data sensitivity an insider can access.
Extremely low frequency but catastrophic severity. Reflects systemic risk from a compromised upstream provider.
High frequency due to human error. Severity depends on the sensitivity of the exposed data.

controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.rationale: Reduces frequency of phishing and credential theft by ~85% based on CISA and industry studies.

controls.name: Zero Trust Architecture
controls.rationale: Reduces frequency of lateral movement and severity of data theft through micro-segmentation and continuous verification.

controls.name: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
controls.rationale: Directly reduces the severity of data theft by detecting and blocking sensitive data exfiltration.

controls.name: Automated Patch Management
controls.rationale: Reduces frequency of exploit-based scenarios (e.g., zero-days or known vulnerabilities).

controls.name: Endpoint Detection & Response
controls.rationale: Reduces severity of ransomware by detecting and stopping encryption in progress.

controls.name: Security Awareness Training
controls.rationale: Reduces frequency of social engineering by improving employee detection capabilities.

controls.name: Immutable Backups
controls.rationale: Reduces severity of ransomware-induced business interruption by ensuring fast recovery.
